title: runtime/observability: add queue delay + batch formation metrics and wire to tracing spans
author: Julian Moore
release_notes:
- Adds queue delay and batch formation metrics for tiered batching rollouts (fast/standard/cost-efficient)
- Adds tracing span annotations for end-to-end tail-latency debugging (queue -> prefill -> decode)
- No API/config changes
description:
Title
Add queue delay + batch formation metrics (histograms + counters) and wire to tracing spans for tail-latency debugging

Context
We’re rolling out tiered batching defaults and need visibility into where tail latency comes from when p95/p99 moves: queueing, batch formation, prefill, decode, or downstream cancellation/timeouts. Today we have only coarse request latency + GPU util; we can’t answer: “Did p95 go up because queue delay rose, because batch size drifted smaller, or because decode starvation increased?”

This PR implements the instrumentation portion of ENG-18422.

What’s included
1) New Prometheus metrics (low-cardinality labels; histogram buckets tuned for p95/p99 analysis)
- redwood_runtime_queue_delay_ms (histogram)
  - Measures: time from admission to being scheduled for prefill (i.e., request sits in the scheduler queue)
  - Record point: at the moment a request is popped into a formed batch (prefill stage)
- redwood_runtime_batch_wait_ms (histogram)
  - Measures: time between batch candidate creation and batch dispatch (covers micro-wait while filling)
- redwood_runtime_batch_size (histogram)
  - Records: number of sequences in each formed batch
- redwood_runtime_batch_tokens_prefill (histogram)
  - Records: approximate prefill tokens per batch (used to detect long-context driven batching collapse)
- redwood_runtime_batches_formed_total (counter)
  - Labels include tier + model_family + route; increments once per batch formation event
- redwood_runtime_queue_admissions_total (counter)
- redwood_runtime_queue_rejections_total (counter)
  - Includes reason label: overload_protection | kv_cache_pressure | max_concurrency | invalid_request
- redwood_runtime_request_cancellations_total (counter)
  - reason label: client_cancel | deadline_exceeded | upstream_timeout

Labels (guarded to avoid explosions)
- tier: fast | standard | cost_efficient (defaults to unknown when tier flag is off)
- model_family: e.g., llama3, qwen2, mistral (family not full model id)
- route: chat | completions | embeddings | rerank (kept intentionally small)
- region: us-east-1 | eu-west-1 | …
- gpu_sku: a10g | l4 | h100 | … (from node metadata)

Notably NOT labeled
- customer_id, api_key, request_id, full model name, prompt length (we bucket prompt length as span attributes only; see tracing section)

2) Tracing wiring (OpenTelemetry)
- Adds child span: runtime.scheduler.queue
  - Attributes:
    - redwood.tier
    - redwood.route
    - redwood.model_family
    - redwood.scheduler.queue_delay_ms
    - redwood.scheduler.admission_result (admitted/rejected)
    - redwood.scheduler.reject_reason (when rejected)
    - redwood.workload.prompt_len_bucket (0-128, 129-512, 513-2k, 2k-8k, 8k+)
    - redwood.workload.streaming (true/false)
- Adds events on existing request span for batch formation:
  - event: batch_formed with attributes batch_size, prefill_tokens_bucket, batch_wait_ms
- Adds link between request spans and a batch span (runtime.scheduler.batch) when sampling allows, to make “which batch did I land in?” debuggable without attaching high-cardinality ids into metrics.

3) Minimal plumbing + tests
- Common metric registry entries + unit tests for label sets (ensures we don’t accidentally add customer_id)
- Smoke test: asserts histograms are emitted under load in the scheduler test harness

Implementation notes
- Queue delay is measured off a monotonic clock captured at admission and recorded when the request is assigned to a batch for prefill. This avoids conflating network ingress time with runtime queueing.
- Histograms use ms units end-to-end. Buckets were chosen to cover fast tier (sub-20ms queueing) through overload cases (multi-second backlog) without forcing frequent re-bucketing.
- For streaming requests, we still measure the same queue delay; cadence issues are not directly measured here (covered in separate work), but these metrics should help correlate cadence regressions with increased queue delay or smaller batch sizes.

Changed areas (high level)
- runtime/scheduler/queue_metrics.*: capture admission timestamp, record queue delay + batch wait
- runtime/scheduler/batch_formation.*: emit batch size/tokens histograms + batches_formed_total
- observability/metrics/defs.yaml: adds canonical metric definitions + label allowlist
- runtime/tracing/spans.*: queue span + batch events/links
- runtime/tests/scheduler_metrics_test.*: validates emission + label constraints

Illustrative snippet
- Recording queue delay when a request is assigned to prefill:
  - queue_delay_ms.observe(now_monotonic_ms() - req.admitted_at_ms)
  - tracing::set_attr("redwood.scheduler.queue_delay_ms", queue_delay)

Screenshots / validation
- Local run (scheduler harness, concurrency=64, mixed prompt buckets) shows:
  - queue_delay_ms p95 ~ 7ms (fast profile params), batch_size median ~ 6
  - when forcing artificial backlog, queue_delay_ms histogram shifts right as expected

Reviewer notes / discussion (summary)
- Sofia Ivanova requested clarifying semantics: queue_delay should exclude prefill compute; updated docstring and ensured we record at dispatch-to-prefill boundary.
- Logan Wright asked for a strict label allowlist and tests preventing future cardinality creep; added a metric definition registry + unit test that fails if new labels are introduced without review.
- Allison Grant suggested renaming “batch_wait_ms” vs “queue_delay_ms” to avoid confusion; kept both but updated naming/README comments to separate “in-queue time” vs “micro-wait to fill batch.”
- Caleb Johnson flagged trace sampling concerns: batch span linking could be noisy; links are added only when both request + batch spans are sampled (no forced sampling) and we avoid storing batch_id in attributes.
- Rafael Mendes requested counters for admission/rejection to support rollback triggers; added queue_rejections_total with reason.

CI
- First run failed: lint (unused import) + flaky scheduler harness assertion (timing-sensitive). Fixed by removing unused import and changing the test to assert non-zero histogram count rather than an exact bucket.
- Final checks: build/test/lint/perf-smoke all green.

Rollout
- Metrics are safe to ship behind existing instrumentation toggles (no behavior changes).
- Dashboards/alerts are handled in eng-platform observability-pack PR (separate).

Checklist
- [x] Metrics documented with units and stable names
- [x] Label allowlist + tests (no customer identifiers)
- [x] Tracing attributes reviewed for cardinality
- [x] Backwards compatible (no config/API changes)

Related
- Linear: ENG-18422
- Companion work: tiered profile selection (ENG-18421) and dashboards spec (ENG-18427)

Merge
Squash merged to main; no backports requested.
